name: A'ou
catalog_citation: He, Yancheng & Luo, Yongxian. 2025. "Gelao: A highly marginalized language of China." Melbourne Asia Review, Edition 21 (3 March 2025). DOI 10.37839/MAR2652-550X21.5. https://www.melbourneasiareview.edu.au/gelao-a-highly-marginalized-language-of-china/
catalog_locator: Online article (unpaginated), section "Grammatical sketch", paragraphs 1-2; saved file our source folder/plain-text extract DIR…
catalog_quote: Ahou is a non-inflectional language, having no inflection of the type found in Indo-European languages. It is a tonal language like Mandarin Chinese where tones distinguish meanings. The language is largely monosyllabic, that is, “one syllable, one meaning”. It has preserved many old phonological features of the Tai-Kadai group, such as the complexity of the initial consonants. It also exhibits some phonological processes such as assimilation with change of syllable rhymes and grammatically motivated tone variations which exhibit features of “word family”, i.e. words that are related with subtle differences in meaning. Ahou has a complex phonological system, with 42 contrastive initial consonant phonemes (sounds usually associated in English with p, b, d and t), and seven single contrastive vowels and 4 distinct lexical tones.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: A'ou (Ahou of Hongfeng, Dafang County) is a lexical-tone language with four contrastive tones on largely monosyllabic morphemes; the first-hand describer says nothing about word stress or accent. No stress rule can be stated from accessible sources.
new_statements.exceptions: None; only 'grammatically motivated tone variations' (tonal morphology/word families) are mentioned.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns syllable-level lexical tone; no word- or phrase-level prominence discussed. The full phonology (Li, Li & Luo 2014 ch. 2 for Bigong/Zoulei; He 2008 for Hongfeng) was not accessible and may discuss prominence in disyllables/prefixed syllables.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes 'Ahou' as spoken in Hongfeng village, Pudi township, Dafang County, Guizhou (the Hongfeng A'ou variety). Glottolog files 'A Grammar of Zoulei' under aoua1234 as well: per the ELAR deposit page (gelao-li-0324) Zou Lei is the Bigong variety (Zhenning County) and 'A Hou' the Hongfeng variety (Dafang County); the two share only c. 55% basic vocabulary and are mutually unintelligible, though both are classed as A'ou/Red Gelao of Guizhou. Not to be confused with Vietnam Red Gelao (Vandu, redg1235), which the Edmondson & Li preprint describes.
